clue.text: Crops If small, insignificant, may be hotly controversial '

definitions.meaning: farm produce dug from the ground, such as spuds

definitions.text: If small, insignificant, may be hotly controversial
definitions.meaning: two idioms: 'small ...' means something trifling, and a 'hot potato' is a contentious issue

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is not a straight synonym but points at two everyday idioms built on the same vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Spuds are a staple field harvest, and the phrases 'small potatoes' and 'hot potato' supply the second, idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Close friends of the Walrus

parts.note: in Lewis Carroll's poem The Walrus and the Carpenter, the Walrus befriends shellfish and then eats them; these shellfish also keep their shells shut tight, so 'Close' is a pun

explanation.surface: Intimate companions of a big tusked sea mammal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' reads as 'intimate' but also hints at shellfish that stay clamped shut. The Walrus lured them along the beach in Through the Looking-Glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's Walrus walks with a band of young bivalves before devouring them, so they are his 'friends'.

clue.text: A plucky Monsieur gets no quarter from a Greek warrior

parts.note: game means brave or plucky, as in 'game for anything'
taken as written
N, north, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A brave Frenchman is shown no mercy by an ancient Greek fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets no quarter' looks like 'is shown no mercy', but it supplies NO plus N, a compass point. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of Mycenae led the Greek host against Troy in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Not the shape to make the Round Table !

definitions.text: Not the shape to make the Round Table !

parts.words: Not the shape to make the Round Table
parts.note: Arthur's table was perfectly circular; a sphere flattened at the poles is not truly round

explanation.surface: This form would never have suited King Arthur's famous furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a spheroid squashed at the poles, which is not a perfect circle or ball.

clue.text: Insist on protocol once among nasty modern modifications

indicators.note: modifications are changes, so these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone insists on correct procedure after unpleasant modern changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' is a link joining the fodder words; ONCE, NASTY and MODERN together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To be formal and observe etiquette strictly is to insist that proper protocol be followed.

clue.text: He had good news for Yuletide night watchmen

definitions.text: He had good news for Yuletide night watchmen

parts.words: He had good news for Yuletide night watchmen
parts.note: the shepherds watching their flocks by night at Christmas were told of the birth by a heavenly messenger

explanation.surface: Someone brought glad tidings to Christmas-time guards on the night shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'night watchmen' suggests security guards, but means the Nativity shepherds; an angel of the highest order fits the bearer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the highest orders of angels, the kind of heavenly being who announced the birth.

clue.text: Drink like a fish ? But not this, surely ?

definitions.text: Drink like a fish ? But not this, surely ?

parts.words: Drink like a fish ? But not this, surely
parts.note: a fish lives in the ocean, but the boozer's idiom is never about taking in the brine itself

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker surely wouldn't swallow this?
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'drink like a fish' means drink heavily; the joke takes it literally, since a sea fish is surrounded by the salty stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean's salty brine is what a sea fish literally drinks, yet nobody swilling heavily means that.

clue.text: State in the manner of graduates

parts.note: a la, from French, means in the style of
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
MA, Master of Arts, is another graduate

explanation.surface: Declare things the way university graduates would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb, but it is a US state. One word, 'graduates', supplies two degrees, BA and MA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty American states, in the Deep South.

clue.text: Is lost, he declares, without one ?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the verb for declaring is wrapped round a numeral

parts.note: states means declares
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man announces he is lost without someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'he who hesitates is lost' makes the definition fair: to waver is, proverbially, to be lost.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'he who wavers is lost' links being undecided with being done for.

clue.text: Is the king back in the country?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back means the king's name is read from end to start

parts.note: Lear is the king of Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: A question whether the monarch has returned home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LEAR into RAEL. 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Middle Eastern nation founded in 1948.

clue.text: Rearrangements of a horse and other animals

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
rams are male sheep, animals other than the horse

explanation.surface: Moving around a horse and some other beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rearrangements' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Words formed by reordering letters are, quite literally, rearrangements.

clue.text: Once again produced fuel in the plant

indicators.note: in places the fuel within the plant's name

parts.note: a reed is a waterside plant
peat is dug and burned as fuel

explanation.surface: A plant has generated fuel a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing or saying something again means it was produced a second time.

clue.text: Downright artist returns to make noisy speech

indicators.note: returns means the artist's abbreviation goes back to front

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword artist
to rant is to speak loudly and wildly

explanation.surface: A blunt painter comes back to hold forth loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns RA into AR. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean utter or out-and-out, as in 'arrant nonsense'.

clue.text: Exercising in the morning -this could be funny

indicators.note: 'in the morning' means with the morning's abbreviation put in front; remove it from the comic word

parts.note: amusing means funny
AM, ante meridiem, is the morning

explanation.surface: Working out early in the day could be a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: With AM before it this word becomes AMUSING (funny), so take AM away. '-this could be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Using a skill or power is exercising it, as in 'exercising one's right'.

clue.text: Like a creditor not thwarted by such a cheque?

definitions.text: Like a creditor not thwarted by such a cheque?

parts.words: Like a creditor not thwarted by such a cheque
parts.note: a cheque without two parallel lines can be cashed over the counter, so a creditor holding it is not blocked; 'not thwarted' is also the plain sense

explanation.surface: A lender is not frustrated by a certain kind of payment.
explanation.walkthrough: In British banking, crossing a cheque restricts it to deposit into an account; one without the lines can be cashed at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Being not thwarted is being unopposed, and an open cheque lacks the parallel lines drawn across it.

clue.text: Manager in tribe under canvas

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: 'under canvas' means sheltering inside a tent, so the tribe goes within it

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas
Dan is one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: A boss is staying with a tribe camping out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under canvas' is the idiom for camping, so DAN sits inside TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a title for an administrator, especially the director of an opera house.

clue.text: Just over 500? The call appears vacillating

parts.note: DI is 501 in Roman numerals, just over D (500)
taken as written
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: Barely more than five hundred? The phone call seems hesitant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being indecisive, wavering between choices, is vacillating.

clue.text: Ran miles in order to get drinks

indicators.note: put in order means arranged, so these letters are sorted into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone jogged a long way to earn some refreshments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link. In Britain 'minerals' are fizzy soft drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage carbonated soft drinks are called mineral waters.

clue.text: Agrees with many an odd decision

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, many

indicators.note: odd means strange, so these letters are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: Someone concurs with plenty of a strange ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that match or correspond are said to agree.

clue.text: Just a moment — it's urgent

definitions.meaning: a moment is a split second, a tick

explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a link joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a split second and an adjective for something demanding at once.

clue.text: Andromeda takes the lead

definitions.meaning: a constellation, a group of heavenly bodies, so plural in sense
plays the main role in a show or film

explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation of luminous points in the sky, and a headliner has top billing.

clue.text: Do a turn badly in this building

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put together poorly, in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Someone performs a clumsy pirouette inside an edifice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a round building, typically with a dome.

clue.text: It helps to offer returns to bunny-chasers

definitions.text: It helps to offer returns to bunny-chasers

indicators.note: the run of letters in the words that follow helps form the answer, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Something assists in providing a good haul to rabbit hunters.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'offer returns'. As a whole, the clue describes the small animal that drives rabbits from burrows for hunters.
explanation.definitionFit: A domesticated polecat is used to flush rabbits from their warrens for hunters.

clue.text: Part of cricket field — right place for a footballer

definitions.meaning: the leg side of a cricket field, behind the batsman's legs
a footballer not beyond the last defender is legally positioned

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the half of the field on the batsman's leg side has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's leg side has this other name, and a soccer player in a legal position is not offside.

clue.text: Steelmen ordered eg iron and carbon

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Steelworkers arranged the raw materials of their trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron and carbon are basic chemical substances in the periodic table.

clue.text: Censor Tom's turn for a start, giving direction to players

indicators.note: for a start puts the turned piece at the front
turn means the cat's word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, so Tom's gives CATS
Cato the Elder was known as the Censor of Rome

explanation.surface: A Roman official's moment comes first while instructing performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' makes STAC from CATS; 'for a start' puts it before CATO, the Roman censor.
explanation.definitionFit: This musical marking tells performers to play notes short and detached.

clue.text: Occupies top place but falls audibly

indicators.note: audibly means the word for falling rain is heard rather than written

parts.note: rains means falls from the sky

explanation.surface: A ruler holds the top spot but tumbles in a way people can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch holding the throne is in the top position.

clue.text: Obligations of the French connections

parts.note: du is French for of the
ties are links or connections

explanation.surface: Commitments within French family links.
explanation.definitionFit: Duties are things one is bound to do, responsibilities.

clue.text: A gay hat ruined by the point of a sword

indicators.note: by means beside, so the compass letter is set next to the jumbled hat
ruined means wrecked, so these letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A cheerful hat is destroyed by the tip of a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' and 'of' are links. This is a Turkish curved sword with no guard.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a long Ottoman sabre with a double-curved blade.
